food_page_note_template: This value uses a documented composition interpretation. See {id}.

editorial.scientific_provenance_lead: pending formal acceptance by Larry Callahan
editorial.review_cycle: every material source change and at least annually
editorial.project_scope: This register is a BRAIN Diet project. It is not an FDA or USDA project.

status_meanings.Resolved: sufficient evidence supports the current public treatment.
status_meanings.Provisionally resolved: treatment is defensible but remains formulation- or evidence-dependent.
status_meanings.Under review: no public specific value should be inferred yet.
status_meanings.Source withdrawn; research active: an invalid source has been removed and replacement evidence is being sought.
status_meanings.Active rule: a standing identity rule, not a single-food value.
status_meanings.Resolved as rule: a standing identity rule, not a single-food value.
status_meanings.Reference case: retained because it demonstrates an important interpretation rule.
status_meanings.Resolved for named specification: sufficient evidence supports the current public treatment for the named specification.

cases.title: Site-wide ALA mapping
cases.problem: The amino acid **alanine** was mapped to the field intended for alpha-linolenic acid because both can be abbreviated “Ala/ALA.” The false value then entered recipe calculations and omega‑3 totals.
cases.decision: Alanine, beta-alanine and phenylalanine are amino acids and are excluded categorically from ALA and lipid resolution.
cases.action: ALA now requires explicit alpha-linolenic or 18:3 n‑3 identity. Affected food and recipe values are regenerated from corrected source fields.
cases.source_public: USDA nutrient identifiers (1404 = 18:3 n‑3; amino-acid fields are not fatty acids); repository nutrient-identity audit; extraction and recipe regression fixtures.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Alanine, beta-alanine and phenylalanine are amino acids and are excluded categorically from ALA and lipid resolution. **Action:** ALA now requires explicit alpha-linolenic or 18:3 n‑3 identity. Affected food and recipe values are regenerated from corrected source fields.

cases.title: Generic 18:3 fatty-acid records
cases.problem: Some legacy records report only total **18:3**, without distinguishing omega‑3 ALA from omega‑6 GLA or other isomers.
cases.decision: Generic 18:3 remains unresolved and cannot enter ALA or identified omega‑3 totals.
cases.action: Extraction stores USDA nutrient 1270 as unresolved 18:3 and never writes ALA from it. Exact-food analytical evidence may later provide a documented isomer interpretation on a named food page.
cases.source_public: USDA nutrient 1270 metadata; [Golimowski et al. 2022](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#golimowski_hemp_oil_2022); [Goldschmidt and Byrdwell 2021](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#goldschmidt_conjugated_18_3_2021).
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Generic 18:3 remains unresolved and cannot enter ALA or identified omega‑3 totals. **Action:** Extraction stores USDA nutrient 1270 as unresolved 18:3 and never writes ALA from it. Exact-food analytical evidence may later provide a documented isomer interpretation on a named food page.

cases.title: Flax seeds
cases.problem: USDA SR Legacy reports 22,813 mg of unqualified 18:3 per 100 g, while the public page requires a chemically identified ALA value.
cases.decision: The published 22.8 g is USDA’s whole-seed 18:3 milligrams interpreted as ALA. Quantity and isomer identity come from complementary sources, not from one assay.
cases.action: Publish the asterisked 22.8 g row. Store 22,813 mg internally for recipes. Do not publish Foundation 19.42 g (ground seed, different fat) and do not convert an oil percentage into grams of seed.
cases.source_public: Quantity: [FDC 169414](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/169414/nutrients), *Seeds, flaxseed*, nutrient 1270 = 22,813 mg/100 g. Identity: [FDC 2262075](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2262075/nutrients), *Flaxseed, ground*, nutrient 1404 = 19.42 g/100 g, ALA 57.2% of fatty acids against 57.1% in 169414. Identity (literature): [Ribeiro et al. 2013](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#ribeiro_flax_fatty_acids_2013) names alpha-linolenic acid in whole flax seeds; [Gómez-Cortés et al. 2016](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#gomez_cortes_linseed_ala_isomers_2016) runs authentic n‑3 and n‑6 standards on linseed oil and finds only a trace of 18:3 n‑6.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Publish **22.8 g alpha-linolenic acid per 100 g** as a combined-provenance interpretation, not as a single ALA assay. **Action:** The asterisked [ALA row](/docs/foods/flax-seeds#nutrition-row-ala_interpreted) and [source note](/docs/foods/flax-seeds#nutrition-note-ala_interpreted) carry the figure; recipes consume 22,813 mg/100 g internally without duplicating the gram row.

cases.title: Walnuts
cases.problem: USDA reports a large generic 18:3 value but does not identify the omega position in that record.
cases.decision: Walnut-kernel 18:3 is identified as ALA by named GC studies. USDA’s 9,080 mg is the quantity for this page.
cases.action: Publish 9.08 g ALA*. Do not wait on Foundation 1404 (absent). Do not substitute Yoshinaga-Kiriake’s derived milligrams for USDA’s kernel quantity.
cases.source_public: Quantity: [FDC 170187](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/170187/nutrients), *Nuts, walnuts, english*, nutrient 1270 = 9,080 mg/100 g. Identity: [Kafkas et al. 2017](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#kafkas_walnut_fatty_acids_2017) names alpha-linolenic acid across ten *Juglans regia* cultivars (9.50–13.26% of fatty acids) against a 37-component FAME standard; [Yoshinaga-Kiriake et al. 2022](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#yoshinaga_kiriake_walnut_oil_2022) names α-linolenic acid (C18:3n3) against the same standard, which carries n‑3 and n‑6 as distinct components. Rejected for identity: [FDC 2346394](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2346394/nutrients) (fatty-acid totals only; no nutrient 1404).
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Walnut-specific GC studies identify the 18:3 as ALA; USDA supplies the whole-kernel quantity. **Action:** Publish **9.08 g ALA per 100 g*** on the [ALA row](/docs/foods/walnuts#nutrition-row-ala_interpreted). Do not treat Foundation FDC 2346394 as identity (no nutrient 1404) and do not derive the gram figure from oil × fraction arithmetic.

cases.title: Hemp seeds
cases.problem: Hemp can contain both ALA and GLA, demonstrating why generic 18:3 cannot safely be assigned to one omega family.
cases.decision: Hemp 18:3 is a mixture, not a synonym for ALA.
cases.action: Require separately identified ALA and GLA values. Never apply the flax interpretation to hemp.
cases.source_public: [Golimowski et al. 2022](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#golimowski_hemp_oil_2022) (Finola and other cultivars report 18:3 n‑3 and 18:3 n‑6 in adjacent rows).
cases.food_or_scope: Hemp seeds (reference case; no hemp food page yet)
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Hemp 18:3 is a mixture, not a synonym for ALA. **Action:** Require separately identified ALA and GLA values. Never apply the flax interpretation to hemp.

cases.title: Ghee
cases.problem: The cited record contains unqualified 18:3, while animal diet, processing and minor isomers can affect the lipid profile.
cases.decision: Ruminant 18:3 is not a single isomer.
cases.action: Do not publish ALA or include 1,447 mg in identified omega‑3. The milligrams stay internal and unpublished.
cases.source_public: [USDA SR Legacy FDC 173412](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173412/nutrients) nutrient 1270 only; contrast [butter FDC 173430](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173430/nutrients), which reports nutrient 1404 (0.315 g ALA) beside a larger unqualified 1270 figure.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Ruminant 18:3 is not a single isomer. **Action:** Do not publish ALA or include 1,447 mg in identified omega‑3. The milligrams stay internal and unpublished.

cases.title: Soy
cases.problem: “Soy” can refer to whole beans, cooked beans, flour, lecithin or oil, each with a different composition basis.
cases.decision: Mature raw soybeans are the food on this page. Soybean oil is a different food and may supply isomer identity, not oil grams.
cases.action: Publish 1.33 g ALA* from this seed record. Do not copy the oil’s 6.789 g/100 g onto soy, tofu, natto, miso or tempeh.
cases.source_public: Quantity: [FDC 174270](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/174270/nutrients), *Soybeans, mature seeds, raw*, nutrient 1270 = 1,330 mg (6.7% of 19.94 g fat). Identity: [FDC 171411](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/171411/nutrients), *Oil, soybean, salad or cooking*, nutrient 1404 = 6.789 g/100 g and nutrient 1321 (GLA) = 0. The oil’s ALA share is 6.8% of fat — USDA agreeing with itself on proportion, not a transferred quantity.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Resolve the exact food form first. Oil fatty-acid percentages cannot be transferred as oil grams onto whole soy. **Action:** For mature raw soybeans, publish **1.33 g ALA per 100 g*** from this seed record’s 18:3 milligrams, with isomer identity from USDA soybean oil nutrient 1404. The oil’s 6.789 g/100 g is not copied onto the seed page.

cases.title: Avocado oil
cases.problem: A generic 18:3 value does not state its isomer, and composition varies with cultivar, extraction and refining.
cases.decision: Fernandes’ “linolenic (C18:3)” does not resolve n‑3 versus n‑6. Cultivar and refining change the oil.
cases.action: Keep 957 mg unresolved. Do not publish ALA. Do not copy avocado-fruit 1404/1321 quantities onto the oil.
cases.source_public: Quantity: [FDC 173573](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173573/nutrients), *Oil, avocado*, nutrient 1270. Identity attempted: [Fernandes et al. 2018](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#fernandes_avocado_oil_2018) — wording rejected for isomer resolution. Not transferred: avocado fruit [FDC 171705](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/171705/nutrients) nutrient 1404 = 0.111 g and 1321 = 0.015 g.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** “Linolenic (C18:3)” does not identify n‑3 versus n‑6. **Action:** Retain unresolved 18:3; do not publish ALA. Avocado fruit is a different food and is not used as a proxy quantity.

cases.title: Salmon roe and Neuroeshot
cases.problem: Roe’s USDA alanine value was stored as ALA and entered the recipe as 214.2 mg of false omega‑3.
cases.decision: The previous ALA figure was alanine. EPA and DHA on this record are explicit n‑3 acids.
cases.action: Suppress ALA. Keep EPA 983 mg and DHA 1,363 mg per 100 g. Identified omega‑3 is the sum of verified n‑3 components only.
cases.source_public: [FDC 175132](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/175132/nutrients), *Fish, roe, mixed species, raw*: nutrient 1278 (EPA), 1272 (DHA). Unqualified 18:3 nutrient 1270 = 6 mg, unpublished. Recipe: [Neuroeshot](/docs/recipes/Snacks/neuroeshot-roe#recipe-nutrition) scales 15 g of that record.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** ALA is suppressed. EPA and DHA remain because their identities and quantities are explicit. **Action:** Identified omega‑3 totals include only verified n‑3 components. The leftover 6 mg of unqualified 18:3 stays unpublished.

cases.title: Total omega‑3
cases.problem: Some totals included corrupted ALA, unresolved 18:3, or were labelled “total” while representing only EPA + DHA.
cases.decision: “Total omega‑3” is not a synonym for EPA + DHA, and it is not a place to park unresolved 18:3 or amino acids.
cases.action: Publish individual acids, the named pair EPA + DHA where that pair is the claim, and a total only when every component is identified and the total equals their sum.
cases.source_public: Food-page `omega3_components` lists. USDA n‑3 identifiers 1404, 1278, 1280, 1272, 1405, 1407. Recipe calculation audit: identified omega‑3 is summed only from those components.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Distinguish individual fatty acids, **EPA + DHA**, and **total explicitly identified omega‑3**. **Action:** Every published total must name its components and equal their sum. Unresolved 18:3 never enters the total.

cases.title: Sunflower lecithin
cases.problem: Sunflower oil was previously used as a substitute record. Native, de-oiled and fractionated lecithins have materially different phospholipid and PC contents.
cases.decision: Sunflower oil is the triglyceride stream after phospholipids have been removed. It cannot describe lecithin.
cases.action: Withdraw the oil panel. Keep phosphatidylcholine and choline as presence-only until a named native or de-oiled specification is declared. Do not call a derived choline moiety a measured total choline.
cases.source_public: Withdrawn: [FDC 1750349](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/1750349/nutrients), *Oil, sunflower* (including its ALA, EPA and DHA). Retained as lecithin-identity evidence, not as a quantity: [Penci et al. 2010](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#penci_lecithin_hydrolysis_2010).
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Lecithin is the phospholipid fraction, not the oil. **Action:** Keep the page qualitative until the documented form is declared. Phosphatidylcholine and choline are presence-only. Derived PC-bound choline must not be called directly assayed total choline.

cases.title: MCT oil
cases.problem: A canola-oil record had been used for a chemically different formulated oil.
cases.decision: Canola is a long-chain seed oil. MCT oil is a formulated C8/C10 triglyceride product.
cases.action: Withdraw canola. Publish energy and fat from a named specification, with the C8:C10 ratio treated as formulation-specific.
cases.source_public: Current: [FDC 2543941](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2543941/nutrients), MCT Premium C8 & C10, declared 60% C8 / 40% C10; 833 kcal and 100 g fat per 100 g. Withdrawn: [FDC 748278](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/748278/nutrients), *Oil, canola* (saturated fat 6.61 g; ALA 7,450 mg). Class definition: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code, medium-chain triglycerides as triacylglycerols predominantly 8:0 and 10:0.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Canola composition is withdrawn. **Action:** Use a named MCT formulation stating energy and total fat, with formulation limitations. Individual C8/C10 milligrams are not published as if they were a universal MCT oil.

cases.title: Algal oil
cases.problem: A canola record had previously been used where USDA had no exact algal-oil composition. DHA-rich and combined DHA/EPA oils are distinct formulations.
cases.decision: There is no USDA SR Legacy algal-oil food. Canola, fish oil and other oils are not proxies. DHA-rich and DHA/EPA oils are different authorised formulations.
cases.action: Publish regulatory specification rows, not a substitute composition panel. DHA leads; EPA is shown only where the combined formulation specifies it. Per-serving milligrams come from the product label.
cases.source_public: [Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2470](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#eu_2017_2470_union_list) (consolidated 25 September 2024). [NIH omega‑3 consumer fact sheet](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#nih_omega3_factsheet_consumer). Absorption context: [Arterburn et al. 2008](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#arterburn_algal_2008).
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Use authorised product specifications and label-dose context, not a substitute oil. **Action:** DHA leads the page; EPA is formulation-specific and not assumed universally present.

cases.title: Reishi mushroom
cases.problem: The page cited a beech-mushroom record for a different species. Fruiting body, mycelium, powder and extract are also compositionally distinct.
cases.decision: Beech mushroom is a different species from *Ganoderma lucidum*. No value taken from that record was a measurement of reishi.
cases.action: Withdraw the complete beech-derived panel. Keep polysaccharides qualitative until exact-species, exact-material evidence is attached.
cases.source_public: Withdrawn: [FDC 2003603](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2003603/nutrients), *Mushroom, beech*. USDA SR Legacy has no reishi record. Replacement must be *Ganoderma* analytical literature with material and dry/fresh basis stated.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** A mismatch invalidates the entire derived panel. **Action:** Withdraw the beech-derived panel. Restore only exact-species, exact-material analytical rows. Polysaccharides remain qualitative.

cases.title: Turkey tail mushroom
cases.problem: The page cited a beech-mushroom record for a different species.
cases.decision: *Trametes versicolor* is not beech mushroom. A culinary edible-portion panel would also misdescribe a woody bracket fungus.
cases.action: Withdraw the substituted panel. Keep beta-glucans and polysaccharides qualitative.
cases.source_public: Withdrawn: [FDC 2003603](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2003603/nutrients), *Mushroom, beech*. Replacement must be exact-species analytical literature distinguishing fruiting body, mycelium and extract.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** *Trametes versicolor* is not beech mushroom, and a culinary per-100 g panel would misdescribe a woody bracket fungus even if the species matched. **Action:** Withdraw the substituted panel. Beta-glucans and polysaccharides remain qualitative.

cases.title: Cordyceps
cases.problem: A related mushroom record could not establish Cordyceps composition, and commercial products may represent different species or cultured mycelia.
cases.decision: The beech record cannot establish Cordyceps. Commercial products may be *C. militaris* stroma or cultured mycelium.
cases.action: Keep quantitative composition withdrawn. Keep polysaccharides qualitative until species and material are declared and matched.
cases.source_public: Withdrawn: [FDC 2003603](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/2003603/nutrients), *Mushroom, beech*. Replacement requires named species and named fruiting-body, mycelium or product analysis.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Keep quantitative composition withdrawn until species and material are declared. **Action:** Polysaccharides remain qualitative. Do not reuse the beech panel.

cases.title: Related-food substitution
cases.problem: Some apparently authoritative records described a related ingredient rather than the food on the page.
cases.decision: An authoritative identifier is not enough if it describes a related ingredient.
cases.action: Match food or product, species, edible material, preparation state and formulation. On mismatch, withdraw the whole panel.
cases.source_public: Worked examples: MCT oil vs canola (FCIR-012); sunflower lecithin vs sunflower oil (FCIR-011); reishi, turkey tail and cordyceps vs beech mushroom (FCIR-014–FCIR-016). Document the rejected record on the food page.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** A source must match food or product, species, edible material, preparation state and formulation. **Action:** A mismatch invalidates the entire derived panel, not only the nutrient that exposed it.

cases.title: Tofu, natto, miso and tempeh
cases.problem: Each food’s USDA record reports unqualified 18:3. Oil grams must not be copied onto these foods.
cases.decision: Each food keeps its own USDA 18:3 milligrams. Isomer identity is taken from USDA soybean oil 1404, not from oil grams.
cases.action: Publish the asterisked ALA rows. Leave tempeh’s lower fat share (~2.3% vs ~6.8% in the oil) standing; do not “correct” it toward the oil.
cases.source_public: Tofu [FDC 172475](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/172475/nutrients) 582 mg; natto [FDC 172443](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/172443/nutrients) 734 mg; miso [FDC 172442](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/172442/nutrients) 405 mg; tempeh [FDC 174272](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/174272/nutrients) 248 mg — all nutrient 1270. Identity: soybean oil [FDC 171411](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/171411/nutrients) nutrient 1404.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Same isomer identity as soy oil nutrient 1404; quantity remains each food’s own 1270 milligrams. **Action:** Publish asterisked ALA rows: tofu 0.582 g, natto 0.734 g, miso 0.405 g, tempeh 0.248 g per 100 g. Tempeh’s fat share does not match the oil’s ~6.8% and that difference is left standing.

cases.title: Spirulina
cases.problem: USDA reports 823 mg of unqualified 18:3. Cyanobacterial 18:3 is the inverse flax case.
cases.decision: Cyanobacterial 18:3 is predominantly GLA, the inverse of flax. Treating 823 mg as ALA would invert the omega family.
cases.action: Do not publish ALA. Do not publish GLA from this record either, because the record does not name the isomer.
cases.source_public: [FDC 170495](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/170495/nutrients), *Seaweed, spirulina, dried*, nutrient 1270 = 823 mg; no 1404 or 1321. Page limitations note records the inverse-flax reading.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** Do not interpret spirulina 18:3 as ALA. **Action:** Leave the milligrams unresolved and unpublished. Do not publish them as GLA either, because this record does not name the isomer.

cases.title: Chia seeds
cases.problem: Chia is an ALA-rich seed, but the site still requires an explicit n‑3 identifier rather than an assumed 18:3.
cases.decision: This USDA record already identifies 18:3 n‑3. No overlay is required.
cases.action: Publish 17,830 mg ALA per 100 g from nutrient 1404.
cases.source_public: [FDC 170554](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/170554/nutrients), *Seeds, chia seeds, dried*, nutrient 1404.
cases.interpretation_public: **Decision:** This record already names 18:3 n‑3. **Action:** Publish ALA from USDA nutrient 1404 at 17,830 mg/100 g. No combined-provenance overlay is required.
